title: Illicit Shadows begins pre-production on Illicit Gold
summary: The second investigation follows a single trade from the mud it comes out of to the market that will not ask where it came from: the rush to cash in on the criminal shadows of El Dorado.

body.x: Illicit Shadows, LLC has begun pre-production on its second investigation, **Illicit Gold: the rush to cash in on the criminal shadows of El Dorado**, in partnership with the [International Coalition Against Illicit Economies (ICAIE)](https://icaie.com) and [RAD Original Creations (RADOC)](https://radoc.co).

Gold has never been worth more. An ounce has gone from under $300 in 2000 to more than $5,600 in early 2026, and almost none of it has to say where it came from. In the Amazon, that gap has become an industry: about 80% of mining in the region is presumed illegal, and the trade is valued at $12 to $48 billion a year.

The investigation follows a single trade from the mud it comes out of to the market that will not ask about it: the garimpeiro who mixes mercury with his bare hands and eats fish from the river he poisons, the armed groups who do not dig but sell the diesel and collect the tax, the airstrip no inspector visits, and the refinery where the crime quietly ends and a commodity begins.

That last step is the part nobody talks about. Once gold is refined, no routine assay can establish where it was mined. About 70% of the world's gold passes through refineries in Switzerland, under 2% of shipping containers are ever inspected, and everyone downstream is telling the truth.

Filming is planned across Colombia, Brazil and Switzerland through 2026 and 2027. As with the first investigation, the film will be released free on YouTube, and the evidence behind it will be published alongside it.
Everything is connected.

title: ICAIE announces the creation of the Museum of Illicit Shadows (MIS) as a featured virtual knowledge hub in the fight against illicit economies
summary: ICAIE, led by David M. Luna, announces the digital Museum of Illicit Shadows in partnership with Shadowverse Media and RAD Original Creations, with Sam Rad as co-curator.

body.x: The [International Coalition Against Illicit Economies (ICAIE)](https://icaie.com), led by former U.S. diplomat and national security official David M. Luna, announced today the creation of the digital [Museum of Illicit Shadows (MIS)](/museum), in partnership with Shadowverse Media and [RAD Original Creations (RADOC)](https://radoc.co). Building on the earlier creation of its forthcoming docuseries, Illicit Shadows: The Dark Forces Shaping the Global Underworld (“Illicit Shadows”), ICAIE will be the MIS co-curator, shining a light on the victims of illicit trafficking networks, drug cartels, and other transnational criminal organizations (TCOs).
ICAIE is proud to be associated with futurist and anthropologist Sam Rad (Samantha Radocchia), who will serve as co-curator of [MIS](/museum).

The museum is a first of its kind virtual knowledge hub dedicated to educating global communities on the harms and impacts on international security of crime convergence and illicit economies around the world.

Illicit economies are the lifeblood of today’s bad actors, enabling kleptocrats to loot their countries, criminal organizations to co-opt states and export violence, and terrorist groups to finance their attacks against our societies. Across today’s global threat environment, criminals and bad actors exploit natural disasters, human misery and market shocks for illicit enrichment.
Illicit economies and greed crimes are not harmless and have tremendous human, economic, societal, environmental, and security costs and consequences.

The lucrative criminal activities enabling and fueling the multi trillion-dollar illicit economies include the smuggling and trafficking of narcotics, opioids, weapons, humans, counterfeit and pirated goods; illegal tobacco and alcohol products; illegally harvested timber, wildlife and fish; pillaged oil, diamonds, gold, natural resources and precious minerals; and other contraband commodities. As of 2025, illicit trade has emerged as a Top 5 World Economy (GDP), yielding criminals, bad actors, and threat illicit networks an estimated $3-5 trillion a year.

From the dense forests of the Amazon to the bustling ports and free trade zones around the world, from the cyber battlegrounds of Eastern Europe to the hidden safe financial havens of the West, the Illicit Economies of The Shadowverse reveal the complex web of interactions and influences that drive illicit trade and impact global security.

Joining forces and energies, ICAIE and Illicit Shadows, LLC envision the [Museum of Illicit Shadows](/museum) as an information hub on the growing threats posed by illicit economies, examining how crime convergence impacts all communities through exhibitions, research, dialogues, public programming and investigative docuseries films.

In an era marked by escalating global challenges, our mission is not just to expose the dark commerce of this parallel universe, but to shine a light so that through understanding and awareness, we can collectively illuminate the world, fostering cooperation, public-private partnerships, and global action.
[MIS](/museum) online is currently under construction and coming in 2026.
Everything is connected. Join us on our journey into the Illicit Shadows, and support the Museum of Illicit Shadows as a founding donor and benefactor today: [illicitshadows.com/donate](/donate).

title: ICAIE and RADOC begin production on Ep. 01: Chemical Cartels
summary: ICAIE begins scripting the first investigation with Sam Rad and partners including the Council of the Great Lakes Region: cross-border illicit flows, the fentanyl trade, and the dirty money financing further criminality.

body.x: ICAIE has started coordinating with [Sam Rad (Samantha Radocchia)](https://www.linkedin.com/in/samradofficial/) and partners such as the [Council of the Great Lakes Region](https://www.linkedin.com/company/council-of-the-great-lakes-region/), et al, on scripting our first episode of Illicit Shadows (Ep.1: The Chemical Cartels and their Illicit Enablers) of our ICAIE-RADOC docuseries: Illicit Shadows.

We will be examining the scale of cross-border illicit flows, especially the illegal fentanyl and drug trade, and how these illicit markets generate dirty monies that finance further criminalities in Canada, along the border with the United States with a special spotlight on the Great Lakes region, and beyond in places like Australia and across the Americas and Asia Pacific region alike.
Join us on our journey into the Illicit Shadows.
Illicit Shadows are all around us, everywhere. They know no borders. And they encompass the intricate, often unseen networks of illicit trade and criminalized economies that silently shape our world.
